topic: Deal Sheet: four data center loans in five weeks (DayOne, AirTrunk, STT GDC, VIRTUS)

sources.title: DayOne upsizes Malaysia financing to US$7.2 billion; total billings surpass 1GW and bookings reach 2.3GW
facts: DayOne upsized its Malaysia senior secured syndicated term financing for the Johor platform to approximately US$7.2 billion, from approximately US$3.5 billion secured in May 2025
Billings (contracted, income-generating IT capacity) surpassed 1GW, up from 121MW at the end of 2024

sources.title: AirTrunk secures AU$4.25 billion green loan for Sydney data center campus
facts: Headline: AirTrunk secures AU$4.25 billion green loan for Sydney data center campus
Standfirst: current expansion phase for SYD3 site due live in 2028

sources.title: STTGDC secures US$ 590 million green loan for expansion of Tokyo DC campus
facts: STT GDC secured a US$590 million green loan to fit out and operate STTGDC TYO1 and TYO2 in Inzai City, Greater Tokyo
Loan eligibility includes a design PUE of 1.3 or below
Standard Chartered lead coordinator; Mizuho Bank, OCBC, Société Générale and UOB also supported

sources.title: VIRTUS secures £2.45 billion financing package to support continued growth
facts: VIRTUS Data Centres secured a £2.45 billion financing package from 13 banks
Includes a £1.2 billion green capex facility
Funds the 78 MW AI-ready Saunderton campus in Buckinghamshire, further investment at LONDON19 in Slough and expansion across Europe
MW under construction: Japan 1433; Malaysia 1402; Australia 1010; United Kingdom 500 (published capacity only)

caption:
$7.2B: DayOne's upsized Malaysia financing leads four data center loans signed in five weeks.

AirTrunk raised A$4.25B for its SYD3 campus in Sydney. STT GDC closed a $590M green loan for 70.8 MW in Greater Tokyo. In the UK, VIRTUS secured £2.45B from 13 banks.

Three of the four include green-labelled debt.

Data: Coloprice pipeline tracker, 28 Oct 2026. Sources: PR Newswire, DCD, W.Media, Intelligent Data Centres. Details on the last slide.
